gaps.sentence: The film was ___ good, but not brilliant.
gaps.hint: an adverb of degree is needed before 'good'
gaps.explanation: 'Quite' means fairly or rather; 'quiet' is an adjective meaning without noise.

gaps.sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).
'Your' shows possession; 'you're' means 'you are'; 'yours' is a possessive pronoun standing alone.

gaps.sentence: We stayed in Rome ___ two weeks.
gaps.explanation: 'For' is used with a length of time; 'since' is used with a starting point; 'during' is followed by an event or period noun without a length.

gaps.sentence: We ___ money by cycling to work instead of driving.
gaps.hint: to keep money instead of spending it
gaps.explanation: 'Save money by doing something' means to avoid spending it; 'earn' means to receive money for work.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.
